statement_judged: On one CPU of a 4-vCPU cloud VM (Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz; not an isolated lab node, so the seconds are diagnostic), in this harness's implementation (std HashMap with SipHash), 36 configurations (the 12 prime-order Weierstrass curves of the v5 study, group orders about 2^24, 2^28 and 2^32, with a new seed; T = 1024/4096/16384) x 17 run keys x 3 interleaved repeats, every target verified: the fastest of four multi-target index-calculus variants per configuration takes 0.78-0.83x the solve-phase wall time of the fastest of ten multi-target rho runs at 2^24 (faster in all 3 cells; 12 of 12 configurations below 1), 0.93x at 2^28 with T = 1024 (faster under the primary rule, but unranked under the pre-registered fixed-key control and 0.98x in the validator's rerun), is unranked at 2^28 with T = 4096 and 16384, and takes 1.11-1.29x at 2^32 (slower in all 3 cells; 12 of 12 configurations above 1). Each cell decision is a 4-of-4 sign rule (the bootstrap interval of the median of 4 equals their range). The pre-registered fixed-key control (0.75-1.28x) is unranked in one cell at each end (2^24 with T = 16384, 2^32 with T = 1024); an independent pinned rerun with the same keys (8 repeats) reproduces all 9 decisions at 0.77-0.84x (2^24) and 1.11-1.22x (2^32). The IC takes 1.33-1.59x the time of a paired BSGS. Measured prices (opcost microbenchmarks; lookups and native operations timed as independent-iteration loops): one affine addition 214-294 ns, I/M 23-31, a canonicalisation plus one hash of x (two counted native operations) 0.005-0.009 GAE and a step index 0.002-0.006 GAE, a std HashMap lookup 0.04-0.85 GAE at 2^10-2^24 entries.
